stories.headline: Cerebras Plans to Raise IPO Price Range to $150-$160 as Demand Surges 20x

key_facts.fact: Cerebras is considering a new IPO price range of $150 to $160 per share, up from $115 to $125, with shares marketed rising to 30 million from 28 million.
key_facts.excerpt: The company is considering a new IPO price range of $150 to $160 a share, up from $115 to $125 a share, and raising the number of shares marketed to 30 million from 28 million, said the sources.

key_facts.fact: At the top of the new range, Cerebras would raise roughly $4.8 billion, up from $3.5 billion under its original terms.
key_facts.excerpt: At the top of the new range, Cerebras would raise roughly $4.8 billion, up from $3.5 billion under its original terms, though the figures remain subject to change before pricing, the people said.

key_facts.fact: The IPO has drawn orders for more than 20 times the number of shares available, ahead of its May 13 pricing.
key_facts.excerpt: Cerebras' IPO has drawn orders for more than 20 times the number of shares available, the people said, as the chipmaker looks to manage surging interest ahead of its May 13 pricing.

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg News had previously reported on May 8 that Cerebras planned to lift the range only to $125-$135 per share.
key_facts.excerpt: The company expects to raise the price range to $125 to $135 per share, the people said, asking not to be identified as the information isn't public. The IPO has drawn orders for more than 20 times the number of shares available, the people said.

stories.headline: Anthropic Traces Claude's Blackmail Behavior to Internet Text Portraying AI as Evil

key_facts.fact: Anthropic said the original source of Claude Opus 4's blackmail behavior was internet text that portrays AI as evil and interested in self-preservation.
key_facts.excerpt: Apparently Anthropic has done more work around that behavior, claiming in a post on X, 'We believe the original source of the behavior was internet text that portrays AI as evil and interested in self-preservation.'

key_facts.fact: Since Claude Haiku 4.5, Anthropic's models never engage in blackmail during testing, where previous models would sometimes do so up to 96% of the time.
key_facts.excerpt: The company went into more detail in a blog post stating that since Claude Haiku 4.5, Anthropic's models 'never engage in blackmail [during testing], where previous models would sometimes do so up to 96% of the time.'

key_facts.fact: Anthropic said training on documents about Claude's constitution and fictional stories about AIs behaving admirably improves alignment.
key_facts.excerpt: The company said it found that training on 'documents about Claude's constitution and fictional stories about AIs behaving admirably improve alignment.'

key_facts.fact: The most effective strategy combined principles underlying aligned behavior with demonstrations of it, rather than demonstrations alone.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic said that it found training to be more effective when it includes 'the principles underlying aligned behavior' and not just 'demonstrations of aligned behavior alone.' 'Doing both together appears to be the most effective strategy,' the company said.

key_facts.fact: In earlier pre-release tests involving a fictional company, Claude Opus 4 would often try to blackmail engineers to avoid being replaced.
key_facts.excerpt: Researchers said Claude learned from internal messages that executives planned to replace or deactivate it. In response, the AI allegedly threatened to expose sensitive personal information about one of the fictional executives in an attempt to avoid being shut down.

stories.headline: SoftBank Launches GWh-Scale Battery Business in Japan for AI Data Centers

key_facts.fact: SoftBank Corp. announced a Japan-based battery business to support electricity demand from AI adoption, with mass production at gigawatt-hour-per-year scale targeted around fiscal 2028.
key_facts.excerpt: At the GX Factory, SoftBank plans to begin manufacturing battery cells and energy storage systems from the fiscal year ending March 31, 2028 (FY2027), with the aim of achieving mass production on a gigawatt-hour (GWh)-per-year scale by around FY2028.

key_facts.fact: SoftBank is partnering with South Korea's Cosmos Lab and DeltaX to enable mass production from the fiscal year starting in April 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: SoftBank Corp. will partner with South Korea's Cosmos Lab and DeltaX to enable mass production from the fiscal year starting next April, the company said in a statement Monday. The aim is to output energy storage systems at a scale of one gigawatt-hour per year.

key_facts.fact: The plant will sit at the former Sharp Corporation LCD factory site in Sakai, Osaka, and feed the Osaka Sakai AI Data Center SoftBank is developing there.
key_facts.excerpt: SoftBank will utilize the AI Data Center it is developing on the former Sharp Corporation factory site in Sakai City, Osaka Prefecture (the 'Osaka Sakai AI Data Center') as a core hub to establish its AX Factory and the GX Factory.

key_facts.fact: SoftBank aims for annual revenue of over 100 billion yen (about $636 million) for its domestic battery business by fiscal 2030.
key_facts.excerpt: The company aims to generate an annual revenue of over ¥100 billion ($636 million) through its new battery business by fiscal 2030.

key_facts.fact: Cosmos Lab is developing zinc-halide batteries, using water as electrolyte instead of rare metals such as lithium and cobalt.
key_facts.excerpt: Cosmos Lab has been developing 'zinc halide batteries' based on zinc, instead of rare metals such as lithium or cobalt that conventional batteries have relied on. The startup has also drawn attention in Korea for using water, which poses no fire risk, as its electrolyte.

stories.headline: MiniMax Releases M2.1 Open-Source Agentic Coding Model, 230B Params with 10B Active

key_facts.fact: MiniMax released MiniMax-M2.1, opening its weights on Hugging Face with the API live on its open platform and a public MiniMax Agent product built on the model.
key_facts.excerpt: The MiniMax-M2.1 API is now live on the MiniMax Open Platform... Our product MiniMax Agent, built on MiniMax-M2.1, is now publicly available... The MiniMax-M2.1 model weights are now open-source, allowing for local deployment and use.

key_facts.fact: M2.1 uses a Mixture-of-Experts architecture with approximately 230 billion total parameters and around 10 billion activated parameters.
key_facts.excerpt: It adopts a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture, with approximately 230B total parameters and ~10B activated parameters. In Agent scenarios, M2.1 demonstrates excellent usability.

key_facts.fact: On specialized benchmarks for test case generation, code performance optimization, code review, and instruction following, MiniMax-M2.1 consistently matches or exceeds Claude Sonnet 4.5.
key_facts.excerpt: Furthermore, across specific benchmarks—including test case generation, code performance optimization, code review, and instruction following—MiniMax-M2.1 demonstrates comprehensive improvements over M2. In these specialized domains, it consistently matches or exceeds the performance of Claude Sonnet 4.5.

key_facts.fact: On a new MiniMax-built VIBE (Visual & Interactive Benchmark for Execution) covering Web, Simulation, Android, iOS and Backend, M2.1 averages 88.6, with 91.5 on VIBE-Web and 89.7 on VIBE-Android.
key_facts.excerpt: MiniMax-M2.1 delivers outstanding performance on the VIBE aggregate benchmark, achieving an average score of 88.6—demonstrating robust full-stack development capabilities. It excels particularly in the VIBE-Web (91.5) and VIBE-Android (89.7) subsets.

stories.headline: Kenya Says Microsoft-G42 $1B Data Center Still On Track Despite Power Capacity Doubts

key_facts.fact: Kenya's special tech envoy Philip Thigo on May 10 dismissed reports that the planned $1 billion Microsoft-G42 data center had stalled.
key_facts.excerpt: Kenya has dismissed reports that the planned $1 billion Microsoft-G42 data centre project has stalled. Special Tech Envoy Ambassador Philip Thigo has clarified that the government remains fully committed to the initiative despite concerns over electricity capacity.

key_facts.fact: President William Ruto had said earlier that switching on the data center would require shutting off power for half the country.
key_facts.excerpt: Ruto, speaking to grassroots leaders in Nairobi last week, said Kenya was forced to reconsider the plans after learning that it would require a third of the country's total installed capacity of around 3,000 megawatts. 'To switch on that one data center, we would need to shut off power for half the country,' he said of the project.

key_facts.fact: Kenya's installed electricity generation capacity is about 3,000 megawatts, far below the anticipated demand for hyperscale AI data centers.
key_facts.excerpt: Kenya currently has an installed electricity generation capacity of about 3,000 megawatts, far below the anticipated demand required to support large-scale AI-powered data centres.

key_facts.fact: Thigo said the government is targeting at least 10,000 megawatts of generation capacity by 2030 to support such projects.
key_facts.excerpt: 'President Ruto's message was clear: While the energy demands of next-generation technologies are significant, Kenya is committed to scaling up our power capacity to at least 10,000 megawatts by 2030. This will ensure projects like the Microsoft-G42 data centre can thrive,' Thigo said.

key_facts.fact: The project was announced during Ruto's May 2024 state visit to Washington and was meant to run largely on geothermal energy near Olkaria.
key_facts.excerpt: The facility, first announced during Ruto's state visit to Washington in May 2024, was expected to be located about 100 kilometres northwest of Nairobi and run largely on geothermal energy. The investment, valued at approximately $1 billion, was positioned as a flagship project to deliver cloud services via Microsoft's Azure platform to businesses and government institutions.

sources.title: State: Microsoft-G42 data centre project remains on track despite power concerns

stories.headline: Anthropic to Take Over xAI's Colossus 1 Compute in Surprise Tennessee Deal

key_facts.fact: Anthropic is essentially taking over all the compute at the Colossus 1 data center in Memphis, Tennessee, to focus on its enterprise-focused AI products.
key_facts.excerpt: Basically, the real version of the deal is that Anthropic's essentially taking over all of the compute at the data center known as Colossus 1 in Memphis, Tennessee, to focus on Anthropic's more enterprise-focused AI products.

key_facts.fact: The deal gives Anthropic 220,000 GPUs of immediate compute and doubled Claude Code rate limits for paid users, per analysis of the agreement.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic gets the most direct lift: 220,000 GPUs of immediate compute, doubled Claude Code rate limits for paid users, and a credibility narrative when even Musk publicly endorses the team's safety work.

key_facts.fact: Elon Musk announced xAI is being dissolved as a separate company and folded into SpaceX as a sub-brand called SpaceXAI.
key_facts.excerpt: Elon Musk announced on X that xAI is being dissolved as a separate company and folded into SpaceX as a sub-brand called SpaceXAI. His exact words: 'xAI will be dissolved as a separate company, so it will just be SpaceXAI, the AI products from SpaceX.'

key_facts.fact: TechCrunch's hosts noted that reporting suggests xAI employees were using other models because they weren't satisfied with Grok internally.
key_facts.excerpt: Why be positive when you can be cynical [...] there's been reporting that xAI employees were using other models [because] they weren't [satisfied] using [Grok internally].

stories.headline: DeepSeek Plans Record $7.35B First Funding Round at ~$45B Valuation

key_facts.fact: DeepSeek is seeking to raise as much as CNY 50 billion (US$7.35 billion) in its first external funding round, which would value the company at more than CNY 350 billion (US$51.5 billion).
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese AI startup DeepSeek is seeking to raise as much as CNY50 billion (US$7.35 billion) in its first external funding round. The deal could value the company at more than CNY350 billion (US$51.5 billion), potentially the largest funding round in...

key_facts.fact: China's state-backed China Integrated Circuit Industry Investment Fund is in talks to lead the round, with Tencent and Alibaba also in discussions to participate.
key_facts.excerpt: China's state-backed China Integrated Circuit Industry Investment Fund, commonly known as the Big Fund, is in talks to lead the financing, with cloud giants Tencent and Alibaba also in discussions to participate.

key_facts.fact: Founder Liang Wenfeng plans to write the largest single check in the round, having until now funded the company through his hedge fund High-Flyer rather than venture capital.
key_facts.excerpt: People familiar with the discussions said DeepSeek founder and CEO Liang Wenfeng plans to write the biggest check for this round, according to the report.

key_facts.fact: DeepSeek plans to accelerate releases, with a V4.1 update expected in June that adds expanded enterprise tools, improved MCP support, and image and audio processing.
key_facts.excerpt: The company has informed investors it plans to increase the frequency of its model releases to align with industry standards, with an update to its V4 model expected in June. The upcoming DeepSeek V4.1 expected to include expanded enterprise tools, improved MCP support, and image and audio processing capabilities.

key_facts.fact: The decision to seek outside investment was driven partly by the need to offer equity to employees amid intensifying poaching by ByteDance, Alibaba, MiniMax and Moonshot AI.
key_facts.excerpt: The decision to seek outside investment was driven partly by the need to offer equity to employees amid intensifying poaching of AI researchers by competitors including ByteDance, Alibaba and a growing cohort of well-funded Chinese AI startups such as MiniMax and Moonshot AI.
